• In the first blank the most appropriate conjunction is '**when**'.
 
• We use when as a **conjunction** meaning **‘at the time that’.**
 
• The clause with** when **is **a subordinate clause (sc)** and needs **a main clause (mc)** to complete its meaning.
 
• If the **when**-clause comes before the **main clause**, we use a **comma**.
 
 
• *Example: (SC)**When** I was young, (MC)there were no houses here.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 4.**​

**So the complete passage is:-*** I have always enjoyed flying. I wasn't afraid **(1) when** my mother and I boarded LANSA Airlines flight 508. Some people had **(2) given up** flying LANSA because of a recent crash. But **(3) mother **and I had a good reason for flying: I had just **(4) finished** secondary school in Lima, and we wanted to **(5) spend** Christmas with my father in our jungle hut. *

• A **conjunction** is a word that connects or joins clauses, words, phrases together in a sentence.
 
• **Conjunctions** are used to coordinate words in a sentence.
 
• Three types of conjunctions are Coordinating Conjunctions, Subordinating Conjunctions, Correlative Conjunctions.

questions.question: **Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.**
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4 i.e. also.**

 
• The sentence is giving both the names of the river, so '**also**' is the right word.
 
• 'It means '**in addition; too**.' 
 
• Hence it means that the Narmada's other name is Rewa.

 
• The other options are eliminated because they are used for the following reasons:
 
 
• Or: used to link alternatives; otherwise; introducing a synonym or explanation of a preceding word or phrase.
 
• But: used to introduce a phrase or clause contrasting with what has already been mentioned.
 
• And: used to connect words of the same part of speech, clauses, or sentences, that are to be taken jointly.
 
 
 
• **Correct sentence**:The Narmada River, also called the Rewa was previously known as Nerbudda.

questions.question: **Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.**
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3 i.e. as.**

 
• The sentence is giving both the names of the river, the name of the river and what was its earlier name.

 
 
• The name Nerbudda is a **noun**. Hence we have to use '**as' as a preposition** before it.
 
• We use 'as' with a noun to refer used to refer to the **function or characteristic** that someone or something has.
 
• Eg:I worked as a waiter when I was a student.
 
• The name of the river is its characteristic.
 
 
 
• The other options are eliminated because:
 
 
• 'so' is used for the consequence, purpose.
